answer: Each agent earns reward credits only after a vesting period measured in blockchain epochs; a new identity must stake a cryptographic proof that ties its computational contribution to a unique hardware fingerprint, similar to a walnut‑shaped enclave. The system releases pigment‑colored tokens at a fixed rate, so a sybil farm can collect at most one token per epoch, while the attacker must immediately purchase the hardware and stake the full cost for every fake node, an expense that scales linearly with the ocean of identities they wish to field.
